details:
Codyseey is a real-time, hardware-accelerated 3D lunar mission browser and digital twin designed for NASA’s Commercial Lunar Payload Services (CLPS) initiative and the Artemis program.

Operating directly in the browser via WebGL and Three.js, Codyseey combines high-resolution NASA Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter (LRO) elevation models with real-time astronomical ephemeris (JPL DE440/DE441). Users can select any primary Lunar South Pole landing candidate (including Malapert A, Mons Mouton, Haworth Crater, Shackleton Rim, Nobile Rim 1 & 2, and Faustini Rim), step through any epoch between 2026 and 2030, and instantly analyze:

  1. Micro-Horizon Solar Illumination: Precise line-of-sight ray-tracing between the sun and local topography to calculate watt-hours generated by vertical (88.5° tilt) solar arrays.
  2. Direct-To-Earth (DTE) Communication Windows: Elevation and line-of-sight tracking accounting for the Moon's 14-day libration cycle to guarantee RF connectivity.
  3. Terrain Hazard & Ground Contact Dynamics: 11-point 3D hull envelope ground-contact physics across rugged slopes, identifying safe landing envelopes (<10° slope) and hazardous crater drops.
  4. Autonomous Shadow-Dodge Traversal Planner: Waypoint routing that maneuvers rovers (such as NASA VIPER or user-uploaded vehicles) to stay within illuminated zones while sampling high-priority Permanently Shadowed Regions (PSRs).

🚀 What Benefits Does It Have?

  • Unified Operational Picture: Eliminates the need to switch between disjointed spreadsheets, GIS servers, and orbital toolkits by uniting topography, lighting, communications, and rover kinematics into one seamless interface.
  • De-risks Extreme Lunar South Pole Missions: The South Pole features sun angles hugging the horizon (-1.5° to +1.5°), creating long, fast-moving shadows that can permanently freeze battery systems. Codyseey flags shadow-trap risks before rovers embark.
  • One-Click Mission Brief Generation: Automatically compiles ephemeris data, line-of-sight link budgets, and terrain safety profiles into downloadable mission dossiers and presentations for science teams.

🌍 What Is the Intended Impact?

  • For Mission Planners & Commercial Space Operators: Provides an agile, zero-install mission design sandbox for CLPS delivery contractors (Intuitive Machines, Astrobotic, Firefly) to plan traverse routes and surface longevity.
  • For Researchers & Educators: Democratizes complex lunar science by turning raw, terabyte-scale NASA PDS datasets into an engaging, interactive exploration platform accessible to universities and students worldwide.

🛠️ Tools, Coding Languages, Hardware & Software

  • Frontend & 3D Graphics Engine: JavaScript / React 18, Vite, Three.js (WebGL hardware-accelerated pipeline), GLSL custom shaders, TailwindCSS, and Framer Motion.
    • NASA PDS Geosciences LOLA (Lunar Orbiter Laser Altimeter) 5 m/pixel Digital Elevation Models (DEMs).
    • NASA LROC (Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter Camera) NAC and WAC polar surface reflectance mosaics.
    • NASA JPL Horizons / SPICE DE441 Ephemeris converted through topocentric Selenographic coordinates (Moon-Centered Moon-Fixed to Topocentric SEZ frames).
    • NASA Moon Trek & USGS Astrogeology cartographic servers.

💡 How Is Your Project Creative & Innovative?

  • "Upload Your Own Rover" (UYOR) Pipeline: Beyond simulating NASA's VIPER and commercial landers (Griffin, Nova-C), users can drag and drop custom 3D CAD/GLB models. The browser computes real-time wheel contact angles, chassis pitch/roll stability, and solar harvesting profiles tailored to their custom vehicle geometry.
  • Interactive 2026–2030 Solstice Fast-Forward: Built-in intelligence markers guide users to critical mission milestones, including the peak Southern Summer Solstice window (+480W illumination) and maximum Earth elevation (+8.2° DTE lock).

🧭 What Factors Did Our Team Consider?

  • Lunar Topographical Reality: Grazing illumination angles cause crater rims tens of kilometers away to cast massive shadows. We implemented true horizon elevation profiling rather than simple flat-plane astronomical trigonometry.
  • Thermal & Battery Survival Limits: Modeled realistic 120-minute maximum shadow survival constraints for polar rovers.
  • Accessibility & Performance: Designed the 3D pipeline to run smoothly at 60 FPS on everyday consumer laptops and workstations without requiring high-end dedicated GPU clusters.
